# Data Domains main **Data Domains** transform technical models into business-friendly and business-facing portals for data discovery, data governance, quantitative reports, and end-to-end lineage analysis. A Data Domain is a portal for searching, browsing, querying, exploring lineage, and quantitatively analysing *across multiple models*. Each domain publishes content and builds cross-model lineage from the set of models you choose to include. Each Data Domain includes an integrated **Data Map** — a specialised lineage exploration and visualisation tool that automatically aggregates lineage across published models and presents fine-grained, technical data flows in high-level, business-friendly visual summaries. *** Key benefits of Data Domains: * **Familiar search portal experience across multiple models**: Find and analyse data and infrastructure using an interface as intuitive as web search or file browsing * **Business-friendly discovery**: Make technical systems discoverable and understandable through widely recognised and familiar business terms * **Cross-model lineage**: Use Data Maps to visualise end-to-end data flows across multiple models with business context * **Quantitative insights**: Generate Analytics reports for data-driven analysis of your lineage and governance landscape *** This documentation is organised around two primary user roles:
Domain BuildersSet up Data Domains as shareable organisational resources. Domain Builders need deeper knowledge of Solidatus models and domain configuration. Start with Understand Data Domains, Model Architecture for Domains, Configure a context model, and Create a Data Domain.
Domain ExplorersUse domains to explore, find, understand, and analyse data and lineage. See the Explore Data Domains section and sub-pages for guidance on navigating and using domains. For a better understanding of how Data Domains work, see Understand Data Domains.
{% hint style="success" %} Domain Builders should also understand how content from models surfaces to Domain Explorers to create better user experiences for their organisation. {% endhint %}
